decisions.reason: Organic sliced ham fits the firm's stated strategy of expanding organic lines, sits close to its core offer, and a large firm in a growing industry has the slack to keep it despite no evidence of results after 2019.
Organic Kasseler is a low-cost extension of the organic range and its own core production, so there is no clear shortfall that would trigger search for other uses of the resources.
Organic pepper salami uses existing maturation know-how and supports the organic growth direction, making it likely to meet modest aspirations.

The exotic teriyaki aspic is a niche deli-counter specialty with uncertain demand and so has the highest risk of falling short, but available slack and its showcase value make keeping it slightly more likely.
Fennel salami was given its own website page, which suggests the firm saw it as a featured product close to its core salami business, so it is likely judged satisfactory.
A classic liver pâté with veal is a traditional staple that matches the firm's heritage recipes and customer expectations, giving little reason to drop it.
